data.name: Mechanic Miner
data.detailed_description:
Mechanic Miner is a construction and survival game where you build mechanical steam-powered machines in a physics-based sandbox. Gather resources, kill monsters, acquire new technologies and use your imagination to build crazy mechanical devices to conquer challenges.


Mechanic Miner lets you design and construct any kind of machine! From the basic vehicle covered in deadly spikes or the trustworthy catapult to a submarine, an air balloon or a giant mechanical spider.

Mechanic Miner has more than 70 different parts and building blocks for you to play around with and build machines from – all of it simulated through a realistic physics engine making your constructions behave like in real life.

Get creative, improve your skills, build more advanced contraptions and become a mechanical mastermind to conquer any challenges that may lie ahead. You can also share your designs with your friends through the Steam Workshop!


You’re stranded on a strange and treacherous planet where survival is made difficult by hostile animals and plant life. Luckily, you brought a multitool from your home planet that enables you to craft any kind of machine part – provided that you find and gather the right raw materials.

Relying solely on the technology you brought, you set out to explore this new and unknown world. However, your new home planet will not only challenge you – it might kill you! Face waves of deadly critters and fight unrelenting monsters that show no mercy. To survive, you must acquire the necessary steam-powered technology allowing you to delve deeper into the diverse biomes of the planet and perhaps, ultimately, escape.


Let your inner mechanic shine in Creative Mode. With unlimited resources at your disposal, immortality and the ability to fly you can create anything and set your imagination free!

Creative Mode is great for players who want to let their creativity flow without limitations, and with the blueprint tool you can easily save a copy of your contraptions and use them in Story or Survival Mode if you have the resources for it.


Follow your own path in Survival Mode. You start with nothing and explore, gather, research, construct and fight for your survival.

Survival Mode offers new challenges for advanced players – you need to use your wits and imagination to create contraptions that are able to withstand the harsh environment, aggressive enemies and devastating Aether Storms that wreak havoc on the planet.


  • Explore a randomly generated sandbox. Dive into the story, fight for your survival or start creating without limits.
  • Mine the planet for useful resources and start constructing your own unique mechanical steam-powered machines and devices.
  • A realistic physics engine powers Mechanical Miner's sandbox and will test your contraptions’ ability to navigate the harsh terrain.
  • Use your mechanical constructions to fight and defend you and your base from deadly critters and fight unrelenting monsters. Will you survive?
  • Create blueprints of your mechanical constructions and use them in Story or Survival Modes. Or share them with friends on Steam Workshop to prove who the real mechanical mastermind is.
  • Acquire new technologies and expand your base and building capabilities as you progress in the game.

reviews.review:
[h1]Overview[/h1]
[b]Mechanic Miner[/b] is a side-scrolling adventure sandbox set on Mars. Impersonating an engineer named John, players will need to survive in an hostile environment after crash-landing in the wilderness. With most equipment and projects lost, it will be up to you to take it all back, building increasingly advanced machines and facing enemies in the process, with the final objective of either surviving or escaping, depending on the game mode. 

🟩 [b]Pros[/b]
[list]
[*]Complex but relatively easy to use building system, featuring many different parts, weapons and machinery. 
[*]Engaging formula that combines overcoming environmental dangers with combat, scavenging and powerful bosses. 
[*]Two additional game modes apart from Story: Survival, a free roam mode without story quests, and Creative. 
[*]Complete freedom of approach to all obstacles, with player creativity put at the center of gameplay. 
[*]Surprisingly low amount of bugs, considering the freedom and complexity the building system allows.
[/list]
🟥 [b]Cons[/b]
[list]
[*]Tutorials are lackluster: several game mechanics, functions and tools are poorly explained, or not mentioned at all.
[*]Exploration is too linear, with most environments being corridor-like instead of more complex areas.
[*]The low level of interaction with the environment, complete inability to dig terrain or destroy anything can be disappointing.
[/list]
[h3]Rating: Good[/h3]
[url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2548409603]Click here for the complete Rating Chart[/url]

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2013987202

Let's start with the good points. First of all, Mechanic Miner's parts variety used in building your own custom machines is very good: servo-motors, pressure tanks, machineguns, bombs, tesla coils... you name it and probably at some point you'll find it or think a way to jury-rig it. Improvising and making the most of what tech you have at the moment is a crucial part of gameplay, that combined with scavenging material deposits, fighting enemies and bosses, creates enough variety to prevent the game getting stale. 

After completing the story, the presence of two additional game modes, namely Survival which is similar to Story but without quests, optional resource loss on death and a new dungeon for advanced players - and Creative, which is a sandbox with unlimited resources to build anything you want - boosts content amount. The fact you can approach any challenge as you want is great as the game will never force you to use a specific way to solve problems.

On the bad side, the most evident issue is that tutorials are insufficient, and while they explain some mechanics and basics decently, they also leave players blind to many others that are not at all intuitive to figure out: for example I never realized how to use material for module research, because it was never explained properly. The exploration is linear and mostly performed in tunnels or corridors, without much side areas to discover, and this is a letdown.

[b]Overall Mechanic Miner is a good sandbox adventure game that delivers a fresh take on this genre with a good degree of polish and content, but not without some flaws. It took me 14 hours to complete the main campaign, with optionally also Survival and Creative to get into after that. For 16,70€ and with overall good quality, I can recommend this game for full price.[/b]

[quote]Liked this review, and want to see more of the same quality? Check out [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/39323490]Tamaster's Review Archive[/url] to see all my Reviews in a single, convenient location.[/quote]

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2014714830

[h1]In-Depth Breakdown[/h1]
🎮 [b]Gameplay Analysis[/b]
The gameplay of Mechanic Miner is divided into Exploration, Building, Quests and Combat.

[b]Exploration[/b] 
Can be performed on foot, but most of the time will be done while driving your own machine. The environments are not open but instead very linear most of the time, with few optional areas, so exploring thoroughly won't even be a problem since everything is put before you. While roaming, collecting all the various material deposits is fundamental to prevent shortages, as it is with plants and even enemy corpses, giving out many different resources.

Fast travel at every "gate" allows you to quickly reach any previous depth level, in case you need more resources that respawn with time - or deposit materials if you built a stationary base. Checkpoints allow you to save your vehicle and progress in case of defeat or destruction, but also traditional manual saves and autosaves are present. The world map is useful to get a direction. 

[b]Building[/b]
Is the prime activity in the game, and is done very organically because you'll need to connect pipes, belts, tubes and circuits in a realistic manner to make everything work, respecting the laws of physics. At first it can seem very complex and obscure but in fact it is quite handy and well done after getting a hand of it. Creating flying machines, armored vehicles or mobile bases are all very possible things, and building many different vehicles you can save as blueprints, will be key to pass the diverse obstacles.

As you kill new enemies or harvest new resources blueprints are unlocked to make new technology, but in the end how you approach things and what you build is always up to you. Too bad for the lacking tutorials and the control system, as jamming in a 2D plane multiple layers of circuits and pipes is inevitably clunky, as is clunky driving vehicles with many functions or machines, having to swap many control levers constantly. With some effort though, all can be done.

[b]Quests[/b]
Can be primary, story related ones, or secondary typically involving research for optional modules. On the second type, I had no idea how to do so and still don't have any now - since the game never explains it. Often quests involve defeating a boss or recovering a story-related piece of tech. 

[b]Combat[/b]
Will be done mostly with the aid of your machines or fortifications, as John cannot fight on his own apart from a very weak laser beam used to get resources. On the other hand machines you build can have spikes to wound enemies, ballistas, machineguns and other deadly weapons to destroy your enemies. Every weapon can be damaged, destroyed and needs ammo and circuits to be controlled though, so building your machine with this in mind is recommended. 

Bosses are several and each has powerful attacks and phases, most will also summon additional enemies to the fight. In case of defeat, you'll restart from the last checkpoint with everything as new in Story, and also Survival unless you select the optional resource loss modifier. Generally enemies are dangerous but if approached with care and at safe distance they become manageable.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2014824575

🔩 [b]Technical[/b]
[u]PC Specs: RTX2080Ti, Ryzen 3900X, 32GB RAM DDR4[/u]
There are no major problems or bugs to report. A mild stuttering happens sometimes while traversing areas, and a large dip in frame rate when loading after death or returning to checkpoints - but for the majority the game runs smoothly with good stability. Given the simple graphics, the game should run well even on older or low-spec machines. 

[h1]Final Thoughts[/h1]
Mechanic Miner is an unusual take on the sandbox adventure genre that manages to deliver a fresh gameplay and solid content amount for a good price, but also with some issues. Overall a good title that building / sandbox fans will enjoy.

[i]This game was reviewed using a free key[/i]
